Authors: Bai, H.; Zhang, J.; Nowak, R.
Title: AHA: Human-Assisted Out-of-Distribution Generalization and Detection
RQ1: What is the purpose?: OOD generalization and detection through a human-assisted framework by labeling data in the wild.
RQ2 :What methods are used?: AHA: first uses half labeling budget to run a noisy binary search over OOD scores, repeatedly sampling points and asking humans whether they are known or unknown, until it finds the score where semantic OOD and non-semantic data are equally likely. It then spends the remaining budget labeling points tightly around this threshold (the maximum disambiguation region). These labels naturally contain many semantic OOD (helping detection) and many covariate OOD with class labels (helping generalization). Finally, it retrains the classifier with covariate OOD labels and retrains the OOD detector with semantic OOD labels using a joint loss.
RQ2: Categorization: Human in the loop, unknown class handling, Domain generalization

Authors: Zhang, Q.; Feng, Q.; Zhou, J.T.; Bian, Y.; Hu, Q.; Zhang, C.
Title: The Best of Both Worlds: On the Dilemma of Out-of-distribution Detection
RQ1: What is the purpose?: Decoupled Uncertainty Learning (DUL)
RQ2 :What methods are used?: Decoupled Uncertainty Learning: Bayesian perspective and explicitly decouples distributional uncertainty (DU),which is useful for detecting OOD,from overall predictive uncertainty, which is important for generalization. The method increases DU on semantic OOD samples while constraining overall entropy to remain unchanged, thereby avoiding degradation in generalization
SEMANTIC SHIFT: ImageNet-RC, ImageNet-800, TinyImageNet-597, SVHN, Places365, DTD, LSUN (R/C), iSUN, iNaturalist, OpenImages, NINCO, SSB-Hard
RQ7: Metrics: FPR95, AUROC, AUPR, ID ACC, OOD ACC

Authors: Mariani, S.; Klomp, S.R.; Romijnders, R.; de With, P.
Title: The Effect of Covariate Shift and Network Training on Out-of-Distribution Detection
Institution_STD: University of Amsterdam; Eindhoven University of Technology
RQ1: What is the purpose?: evaluate OOD detectors
RQ2 :What methods are used?: rely on superficial feature discrepancies,training choices strongly influence OOD performance, with certain augmentations improving feature discriminability and thus detection, while others can harm it despite improving classification accuracy.
SEMANTIC SHIFT: SVHN, TinyImageNet, LSUN, Places365, CIFAR-100, Textures
RQ7: Metrics: AUROC, Detection Accuracy, Pearson Correlation, TNR@TPR95

Authors: K. Oksuz; T. Joy; P. K. Dokania
Title: Towards Building Self-Aware Object Detectors via Reliable Uncertainty Quantification and Calibration
RQ1: What is the purpose?: unified evaluation framework
RQ2 :What methods are used?: standard object detectors can be adapted into “self-aware” versions by aggregating detection-level uncertainties into image-level decisions (accept/reject), applying proper thresholding, and post-hoc calibration
Models/Backbones: Faster R-CNN, Rank & Sort R-CNN, Adaptive Training Sample Selection, Deformable DETR, ES-RCNN, NLL-RCNN

Authors: Alexey NekrasovAlexander HermansLars KuhnertBastian Leibe
Title: UGainS: Uncertainty Guided Anomaly Instance Segmentation
RQ1: What is the purpose?: combining existing components (Mask2Former + SAM + RbA)
RQ2 :What methods are used?: out-of-distribution segmentation approach (RbA with Mask2Former) to generate uncertainty maps highlighting regions not explained by known classes. From these regions, it samples representative points (via farthest point sampling) and feeds them as prompts into the Segment Anything Model (SAM) to obtain instance-level masks of anomalous objects.

Authors: Wang, Pai-Xuan and Liu, Chien-Hung and You, Shingchern D.
Title: Uncertainty Quantification Based on Block Masking of Test Images
RQ1: What is the purpose?: extends the earlier Block Scaling Quality (BSQ) framework.
RQ2 :What methods are used?: Block Masking Confidence (BMC), an uncertainty quantification method for image classification that estimates prediction confidence by applying sliding random-noise masks to different regions of a test image and analyzing how stable the model’s predictions remain

Authors: F. Lu; K. Zhu; W. Zhai; K. Zheng; Y. Cao
Title: Uncertainty-Aware Optimal Transport for Semantically Coherent Out-of-Distribution Detection
Institution_STD: University of Science and Technology of China
RQ1: What is the purpose?: novel uncertainty-aware framework
RQ2 :What methods are used?: Pathology Image Characterization Tool with Uncertainty-aware Rapid Evaluations, PICTURE integrates multiple foundation models with Bayesian inference, deep ensembles, and normalizing-flow–based out-of-distribution detection to explicitly quantify prediction uncertainty and improve robustness across domain shifts such as different scanners and frozen vs. FFPE tissue preparation.
RQ2: Categorization: Ensemble, Uncertainty and Bayesian evidential methods
RQ7: Metrics: FPR@TPR95, AUROC, AUPR IN, AUPR OUT, CCR@FPRn

Authors: Baek, E.; Park, K.; Kim, J.; Kim, H.-S.
Title: Unexplored Faces of Robustness and Out-of-Distribution: Covariate Shifts in Environment and Sensor Domains
RQ1: What is the purpose?: new dataset to evaluate robustness and ood detection
RQ2 :What methods are used?: ViM, ReAct, ASH, MSP, ODIN
Models/Backbones: ResNet-50, ResNet-152, EfficientNet-B0, EfficientNet-B3, SwinV2-T, SwinV2-B, OpenCLIP-B, OpenCLIP-H, DINOv2-B, DINOv2-G

Authors: Z. Gao; X. -Y. Zhang; C. -L. Liu
Title: Unified Entropy Optimization for Open-Set Test-Time Adaptation
RQ1: What is the purpose?: novel open-set test-time adaptation
RQ2 :What methods are used?: UniEnt first uses a distribution-aware filtering mechanism based on feature similarity and a Gaussian mixture model to separate covariate-shifted in-distribution samples from covariate-shifted OOD samples. applies entropy minimization to known samples to improve classification accuracy and entropy maximization to unknown samples to improve detection, combined with marginal entropy regularization to prevent collapse. UniEnt+, introduces confidence-based weighting to reduce errors from imperfect separation
RQ2: Categorization: Test-time adaptation and filtering, Uncertainty and Bayesian evidential methods
RQ7: Metrics: AUROC, FPR@TPR95, Open Set Classification Rate

Authors: Devi, S.; Dayana, R.; Malarvezhi, P.
Title: Unveiling the unseen: novel strategies for object detection beyond known distributions
Institution_STD: SRM Institute of Science and Technology
RQ1: What is the purpose?: unified OOD generalization framework for object detection (OODG_OD)
RQ2 :What methods are used?: combining pixel-space data augmentation (InterAug for inlier synthesis and FGSM-based adversarial perturbations for outlier simulation), object-level Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) regularization to align in-distribution and OOD feature distributions, and a non-parametric K-nearest neighbors (KNN) scoring mechanism during inference for OOD detection
RQ2: Categorization: Data augmentation and synthetic-shift methods, Post hoc detection scoring
Models/Backbones: Faster R-CNN, Rank & Sort R-CNN, Adaptive Training Sample Selection, Deformable DETR, ES-RCNN, NLL-RCNN

Authors: X Fang, A Easwaran, B Genest
Title: your data is not perfect: towards cross-domain out-of-distribution detection in class-imbalanced data
RQ1: What is the purpose?: new method first closes domain gap and then semantic gap
RQ2 :What methods are used?: Label prototypes to represent each class rubustly and eficiently, Prototype-guided domain alignment aligning target samples with source prototypes, adaptive threshold generation to detect OOD use sample specific entropy thresholds.
